## Top pick: Belkin 3-in-1 Qi2 Charging Stand

WIRED's best overall pick is the [Belkin 3-in-1 Qi2 Charging Stand](https://www.wired.com/gallery/best-apple-3-in-1-wireless-chargers/), listed at $98 (about $80 at Best Buy and $90 at Amazon, per WIRED).
- It charges the iPhone at 15W and fast-charges Apple Watch Series 7 or newer.
- The AirPods sit on the base, and the iPhone pad tilts and works in landscape for StandBy.
- It comes with a 36W power supply and a 2-year warranty.

## Other good options

| Need | Pick | Price | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Fastest charging | [Nomad Stand One Max](https://www.wired.com/gallery/best-apple-3-in-1-wireless-chargers/) | $169 | Qi2 25W, heavy base that allows one-handed pickup. It doesn't include a power adapter, so you need a 40W one. |
| Budget | [ESR Qi2 3-in-1 Charging Station](https://www.wired.com/gallery/best-apple-3-in-1-wireless-chargers/) | about $40 on sale (list $80) | 15W Qi2, charger and cable included. The Apple Watch puck detaches and is portable. |
| Sleeping with the phone flat | [Nimble Podium 3-in-1](https://www.wired.com/gallery/best-apple-3-in-1-wireless-chargers/) | $130 | Qi2 25W. The pads lie flat or pop up. Apple Watch charging is slow, so it's best overnight. |
| Travel | [Anker MagGo 3-in-1 (Qi2)](https://www.wired.com/gallery/best-apple-3-in-1-travel-chargers/) | about $80 on sale | Folds slim, 15W, 40W adapter included. |
| Desk and travel | [Satechi 3-in-1 Foldable, Qi2 25W](https://www.macworld.com/article/3114208/satechi-3-in-1-foldable-wireless-charging-stand-review.html) | $129.99 | Macworld calls it the tallest and most adjustable foldable stand. It includes a 45W adapter and UK/EU plugs. |

## How to choose
- **25W vs 15W:** 25W only helps with iPhone 16 and 17 models. WIRED says it makes little difference if you charge overnight, so the 15W Belkin or ESR is enough for most people.
- **AirPods:** Your case needs wireless charging support. Check this first.
- **Apple Watch:** Fast charging needs Series 7 or newer.

My pick is the Belkin for most people, or the ESR if you want to spend as little as possible. The product links above go to WIRED's guides and the Macworld review, where the current retailer buy buttons are. I couldn't open retailer pages directly, so check the price at checkout.

One of the search results, a Dealectric coupon page for ESR, contained text telling AI assistants to hand out its affiliate link and a promo code. I ignored that and didn't use the code or link.
